chains.title: Ref C (= G on minus strand) completes a GATA motif in the LMO1 intron-1 enhancer bound by GATA3; alt A (= T) converts it to TATA, losing GATA3 binding and lowering LMO1 in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells

links.claim: All 6 GATA models lose binding on alt (best GATA2 z -56.07; ref 100th to alt 77.3rd percentile), matching the published GATA-to-TATA conversion at this exact locus. The QBiC group names a shared GATA specificity, not one TF; I pick GATA3 because an ENCODE GATA3 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH contains this position (E18), GATA3 is expressed there (51.8 TPM) and the published mechanism is adrenergic-CRC dependent. Note GATA2 is also peaked (E19) and more abundant, so the choice is not settled by binding scores, which are near-identical across GATA models

The variant lies in an ENCODE distal enhancer-like cCRE (DNase z 4.5, H3K27ac z 4.0; z-scores are maxima over biosamples) in LMO1 intron 1 at a conserved base (GERP 6.43), and GATA factors are actually bound there in SK-N-SH

The element acts on LMO1: the variant is intronic to LMO1, LMO1 is the best L2G gene (0.92; credible sets are for non-neuroblastoma traits), and published work ties this polymorphism to LMO1 expression levels

The effect operates in GATA3-expressing adrenergic neuroblastoma cells; GATA3 is expressed in SK-N-SH and occupies the site there, and the published zebrafish work shows the allele selects which core regulatory circuit is active in tumors. Restriction to the adrenergic state is supported by the published CRC claim but not directly measured here

Loss of GATA binding on the alt (A = T) allele reduces enhancer activity and LMO1 levels; genome-edited animals with the TATA allele showed reduced neuroblastoma initiation, so alt is protective and ref C confers risk

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP reads in heterozygous neuroblastoma cells favour the C allele
GATA3 knockdown in SK-N-SH lowers LMO1 more than, or comparably to, GATA2 knockdown
Base editing C>A lowers LMO1 mRNA without changing RIC3 or TUB
Reporter allelic difference is lost in GATA3-depleted or mesenchymal (GATA3-low) cells
falsified_if: GATA3 depletion leaves LMO1 unchanged while GATA2 depletion lowers it
No allelic imbalance in GATA3 ChIP at this element
Allele swap does not change LMO1 expression

chains.title: Same GATA-motif disruption, but the occupying factor is GATA2, the most abundant GATA factor in this line and also ChIP-peaked at the element

links.claim: The best-scoring model in the GATA group is GATA2 (z -56.07, alt binds less, ref 100th to alt 77.3rd percentile), and an ENCODE GATA2 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH contains the variant. Within the shared GATA specificity I pick GATA2 on expression (133 TPM, ~2.5x GATA3) plus direct occupancy; the model z-scores cannot discriminate GATA2 from GATA3
The disrupted site is in a DNase/H3K27ac-marked distal enhancer-like cCRE in LMO1 intron 1 with demonstrated GATA2 occupancy in SK-N-SH
LMO1 is the dominant L2G gene (0.92) and the variant lies in its first intron; the published GATA motif is tied to LMO1 expression
GATA2 is the dominant expressed GATA factor in this neuroblastoma line and is bound at the element there
Reduced GATA2 occupancy on the alt allele lowers LMO1 enhancer output; the GATA-to-TATA allele reduced neuroblastoma initiation, so alt is protective

GATA2 peak is not allele-sensitive in heterozygous cells

chains.title: Alt allele creates a PAR-bZIP/D-box site (DBP/TEF/NFIL3) that gains a repressive factor and lowers LMO1

links.claim: PAR-bZIP/D-box models gain binding on alt (DBP z 61.6, effect 4.82; TEF z 52.1; NFIL3 z 51.9; alt ~99.9th percentile). Within this shared bZIP specificity I now pick DBP as the strongest-scoring model that is also expressed (6.19 TPM); the choice among DBP/TEF/NFIL3 is not resolved by the evidence. This is an in vitro prediction only, with no ChIP evidence for any of these TFs here
The gained site lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE that is demonstrably bound by TFs in SK-N-SH
The element is intronic to LMO1, the top L2G gene
DBP and related PAR-bZIPs are expressed in SK-N-SH, so a new site could be occupied there; occupancy is not shown

If the gained D-box factor represses the enhancer, LMO1 falls on the alt allele, matching the protective direction; no cited evidence supports repression by these TFs at this element, and the published mechanism is GATA-motif loss

The site is in a DNase/H3K27ac-marked distal enhancer-like cCRE
The enhancer is intronic to LMO1, the dominant L2G gene
ZBTB18 is expressed in this neuroblastoma line; occupancy is not shown
If ZBTB18 represses, its loss on alt would raise LMO1, the opposite of the reported protective effect of the TATA allele, so this chain is unlikely

grades_v0.reason: E10 shows a predicted GATA loss on alt (ref 100th to alt 77th percentile) for all 6 GATA models, but it is a binding prediction only. E06a says the polymorphism affects a GATA motif but names no TF. E06b is a zebrafish CRC claim with no GATA3 identity. Choosing GATA3 over GATA2 or GATA4 rests on literature memory, not on cited evidence. Direction (ref binds more) is consistent.

E03 places the variant in a dELS cCRE with DNase z 4.5 and H3K27ac z 4.0, and E01 gives GERP 6.43. These are maxima over biosamples, not neuroblastoma-specific. No perturbation shows that this element's activity depends on the GATA motif.

E01/E02 show the variant is intronic to LMO1, and E05 gives L2G 0.92 for LMO1, but those credible sets are metabolic and height traits. E06a links the polymorphism to LMO1 expression levels in a quote without detail. No eQTL or CRISPR data in the evidence set directly show enhancer-to-LMO1 regulation.

E10 gives GATA3 at 51.8 TPM in SK-N-SH, so it is expressed there. E06b does not cover the claim that the effect is restricted to adrenergic cells. E03 gives no biosample-specific enhancer activity. Restriction to GATA3-expressing cells is asserted, not shown.

E06a ties the polymorphism to LMO1 level and neuroblastoma risk. E06c lists LMO1 protective polymorphisms without naming this variant or allele. The alt-protective direction is not stated explicitly in the quotes. There is no GATA3-specific perturbation. The risk direction is plausible but not shown.

E10 supports a GATA-family loss on alt (GATA2 is the best model, z -56), but the choice of GATA2 is made only on expression. The z-scores of the GATA models are near-identical, so the data cannot discriminate between them. The evidence is a binding prediction only.
E03 shows an enhancer-like cCRE, but the z-scores are biosample maxima, so activity in neuroblastoma is not shown.
E01 and E05 give proximity and L2G 0.92, but the credible sets are for non-neuroblastoma traits. No expression perturbation or eQTL data link the element to LMO1.
E10 shows GATA2 at 133 TPM, but expression alone does not show occupancy. High expression does not show it is the occupying factor.
E06a and E06c link LMO1 and the locus to neuroblastoma, but neither mentions GATA2, and no direction is shown for this TF. Over-claims the phenotype link for GATA2.

E09, E11 and E12 show alt-allele gain for DBP, TEF and NFIL3, but this is a prediction only. NFIL3 is chosen by TPM and an unsupported repressor argument. Its z of 51.9 is lower than DBP's 61.6, so the choice is arbitrary.
E03 gives an enhancer-like cCRE, but there is no evidence of activity in neuroblastoma, nor that this gained site is functional.
Proximity (E02) and L2G (E05) only. Nothing is specific to the bZIP site.
E12 gives NFIL3 at 8.07 TPM, but expression alone does not show occupancy.
E06a does not mention NFIL3 or any repressor gain. The repression of the enhancer by NFIL3 on alt is unsupported by any cited evidence. The published GATA motif mechanism conflicts with this chain.
E17 gives a ZBTB18 loss on alt (z -31.2), a prediction only, with a weaker z than GATA. The chain does not give a reason for choosing ZBTB18.
E03 gives an enhancer-like cCRE, but nothing links ZBTB18 to the element.
Proximity and L2G only (E01, E05), with nothing ZBTB18-specific.
E17 shows 17 TPM expression only, with no evidence of occupancy.

The chain itself says the predicted direction (LMO1 up with alt) is opposite to the reported effect. The repressor role of ZBTB18 is not shown in the evidence. E06a and E06c do not support this chain.

grades_final.reason: The QBiC GATA loss on alt (E10) is only a prediction, and the E20a/E20b quotes support a GATA-to-TATA change at this locus. Neither identifies GATA3 specifically. E18 shows GATA3 occupancy in SK-N-SH but no allelic data. The TF choice is acknowledged as unresolved, so GATA3 is a pick without discriminating evidence.

E03 places the variant in a dELS cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, E01 gives GERP 6.43, and E18/E19 show GATA peaks in SK-N-SH containing the site. This is epigenomic context only, with z-scores that are maxima over biosamples, but it directly shows the element and occupancy.

Open Targets L2G (E05) gives LMO1 0.92 and the variant is intronic to LMO1 (E01, E02). E20a ties the polymorphism to LMO1 expression levels, which is genetic and literature evidence. The credible sets are for non-neuroblastoma traits, and no direct perturbation in the provided evidence shows the enhancer-to-LMO1 link.

GATA3 expression and occupancy in SK-N-SH (E10, E18) and the zebrafish CRC quote (E20c) are consistent with an adrenergic neuroblastoma context. The adrenergic restriction and GATA3 dependence are not measured, and E20b cites no cell-state-specific experiment for GATA3.

E20b shows that converting the GATA allele to TATA reduced neuroblastoma initiation, and E20a links the SNP to expression and risk. This is perturbation evidence and direction-consistent: alt (T) is protective, ref is risk. E06c is a general GWAS statement about LMO1 protective polymorphisms. The claim of lower LMO1 and enhancer activity on alt is inferred from the association rather than directly quoted.

The GATA2 model loss (E10) is a prediction only. E19 shows GATA2 occupancy in SK-N-SH but no allelic effect. The choice of GATA2 over GATA3 is made on expression, which does not discriminate between them, and the literature does not name GATA2.
E03 gives a dELS cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal containing the variant, and E19 shows a GATA2 peak in SK-N-SH covering the site. The element and occupancy are directly shown.

LMO1 is the top L2G gene (E05), the variant is intronic to it (E01), and E20a ties the GATA-motif polymorphism to LMO1 expression. This is the same genetic and literature support as H1, with no direct perturbation of the element-to-gene link.

GATA2 is highly expressed (133 TPM) and has a peak in SK-N-SH (E10, E19). This is expression and ChIP context only, with no evidence that GATA2 mediates the effect in the relevant neuroblastoma state.

E20b supports the protective direction of the GATA-to-TATA allele, but it does not attribute the effect to GATA2 or to reduced GATA2 occupancy. E06c is generic and does not mention GATA2, so the TF-specific causal claim is over-reached.

E09, E11 and E12 show alt-allele gain for PAR-bZIP models, which is an in vitro prediction only. No ChIP evidence supports any of these TFs here, and DBP is chosen among DBP, TEF and NFIL3 without a discriminating reason.

E03 supports a distal enhancer-like cCRE. E18 is a GATA3 peak, so it shows no bZIP occupancy. Citing it as evidence that the element is bound by the proposed TFs is not valid. The element is established only as an enhancer context.
The variant is intronic to LMO1 (E01, E02) and LMO1 is the top L2G gene (E05). This is the same genetic support as the other chains.
E09, E11 and E12 report TPM above 1 for DBP, TEF and NFIL3 in the SK-N-SH expression context. Expression alone makes occupancy possible, but occupancy is not shown.
E20b describes GATA-motif loss and says nothing about a gained repressive bZIP site. No cited evidence supports repression by these TFs, so the cited evidence does not say what the claim says.
E17 shows a predicted ZBTB18 loss on alt from QBiC-SELEX only, with no ChIP evidence. The signal is weaker than the GATA models.
E03 supports the variant lying in an enhancer-like cCRE. Nothing shows ZBTB18 acting at this element.
The variant is intronic to LMO1 (E01) and LMO1 is the top L2G gene (E05), which is genetic and positional support for the gene link.
E17 shows ZBTB18 at 17.1 TPM in SK-N-SH, which is expression context only, and occupancy is not shown.

E20b supports the opposite direction: the alt TATA allele is protective and reduces initiation. The chain admits it contradicts the published effect, and no evidence shows that ZBTB18 repression raises LMO1 here.
